why: UNIVERSES: lemma_16_2_2 at 0 (T(Z,c) : Type 1). A: (i) every Tα is a homeomorphism for the instance topology tangentSpaceTopology; (ii) any topology making ONE Tα a homeomorphism is the instance; (iii) the instance is metrizable. B: there is exactly one topology making EVERY Tα a homeomorphism, and every such topology is metrizable. A_to_B: τ := the instance, uniqueness by (ii) at c.out, metrizability via (ii) then (iii). B_to_A: B does not name its topology, so the link 'the instance makes every Tα a homeomorphism' comes from the non-item lemma isHomeomorph_tangentMap (the same lemma the project's proof of (i) uses); (ii) from B's uniqueness after showing one Tα homeomorphic ⇒ all are (Tβ = Tα ∘ |Th|, tangentMap_comp, isGeneralizedIso_tangentHom); (iii) from B's metrizability. A's uniqueness clause is formally stronger (one Tα instead of all) but follows, so the two say the same thing.
